headline: Grand River Conservation Authority Entry and Activity Permits
reservation: Admission is governed by the Grand River Conservation Authority (GRCA), which may require day-use permits or have capacity limits. Specialized activities like tubing or camping require separate, specific reservations that often sell out weeks in advance during the summer. Always check the official GRCA website for the most current booking requirements and water flow status.

days.title: Gorge Heights and River Flows

stops.name: Elora Gorge Lookout
stops.detail: View the 22-metre high limestone cliffs from the safety of the fenced overlooks along the scenic trail.

stops.name: Hole in the Rock
stops.detail: Navigate the unique staircase and rock formation that provides a close-up look at the vertical gorge walls.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes for local transfers; conditions vary by pedestrian traffic.
days.note: Footwear with good grip is essential for the limestone trails which can be slippery when damp.

days.title: River Activities and Mill Ruins
days.start: Suggested: 10 AM from the Conservation Area Gate

stops.name: Grand River Tubing Launch
stops.detail: Participate in the popular local tradition of floating through the gorge rapids (subject to water level safety).

stops.name: Tooth of Time
stops.detail: Observe this iconic rock formation located in the middle of the river near the historic Elora Mill.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes for internal park transit; conditions vary.
days.note: Tubing is strictly dependent on river CFS (cubic feet per second) measurements; check the status daily.

days.title: Elora Quarry and Village Charm

stops.name: Elora Quarry
stops.detail: Visit the 'old swimming hole' surrounded by sheer cliffs for a relaxing afternoon in the sun-warmed water.

stops.name: Elora Mill and Bridge
stops.detail: Walk across the bridge for the classic view of the falls and the historic limestone architecture of the village.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes for parking and village transit; conditions vary.
days.note: The Quarry requires a separate timed-entry ticket from the main Gorge area; verify arrival windows.

intel.title: Limited Village Spaces
intel.text: Parking within the Conservation Area is managed by the GRCA; once full, visitors must find municipal lots in Elora. Village parking is often time-limited and strictly enforced on weekends.

intel.title: Reliable Urban Signal
intel.text: Cellular service is excellent throughout the Elora and Fergus area. Signal may weaken slightly at the very bottom of the gorge near the river level.

intel.title: Local Stations
intel.text: Full services and fuel are available in the immediate vicinity of Elora and the neighboring town of Fergus. You do not need to carry extra fuel for this region.

intel.title: Water Level Access
intel.text: River activities are frequently closed in May due to high spring runoff or in late August due to low water. Check the GRCA water flow dashboard before planning a river-based trip.

intel.title: Timed Entry Systems
intel.text: The Elora Quarry and the Gorge may operate under different seasonal access rules. During peak summer weekends, entry is often restricted to pre-purchased permit holders only.

plan.arrival: Arrive via Region of Waterloo International Airport (YKF) or drive from the GTA. Check into local inns in Elora or Fergus to be within walking distance of the trailheads.
plan.vehicle: Any standard vehicle is suitable for the paved and well-maintained gravel roads of the area. Large RVs may find village street parking difficult.
plan.goldenHour: The David Street Bridge provides a sunset view over the Grand River with the Elora Mill and cliffs in the frame.
